adversarialReviewOfTheReplan.q: does a post-processor actually reach the single-character metric, or does it only add a structure tree over fragmented text?
adversarialReviewOfTheReplan.a: it reaches it, but only because of a specific property of pdf-lib's output: every glyph is its own `q BT .. ET Q` with a trailing `T*`, and it is the `T*` that makes an extractor emit a line break. Merging the blocks into one BT/ET while keeping each glyph's own ABSOLUTE Tm removes the line breaks without moving any ink. Verified: 458 of 458 glyph-show operations identical in position, size and glyph.

adversarialReviewOfTheReplan.q: what stops the merge from welding two unrelated words that happen to share a baseline?
adversarialReviewOfTheReplan.a: a positive continuation test, not a proximity test: same font size, same Tm orientation, same baseline to 0.01pt, strictly increasing x, and an x step at most 1.25x the font size. A letter step is 0.5x to 0.9x the size; a word-to-word step is the whole preceding word. Covered by a standing negative test.

measured, not assumed: 458 of 458 text blocks across all three sheets match the single canonical shape, and every other line is a vector operator. The parser REFUSES anything else rather than passing it through, so a future renderer change surfaces as an exception instead of a silently half-tagged PDF.

adversarialReviewOfTheReplan.q: what did the replan lose relative to the in-place version?
adversarialReviewOfTheReplan.a: heading levels and figure alt text. A finished content stream carries no heading semantics and no image description; inferring either would be a guess written into a binding structure. Both are declared in the result object at runtime, not buried in a comment, and both are listed as leave-behind.
